claim: clang-tidy bugprone-not-null-terminated-result: engine/editor/widgets/node_editor_widget.cpp:161 memcpy result is not null-terminated
rationale: This is imgui-node-editor's ConfigLoadSettings two-call protocol, documented in-place at lines 159-161: the first call passes data==nullptr and returns the required size, the second call copies exactly that many bytes. The buffer is length-delimited by contract and the caller never reads past s.size(), so null-termination is neither expected nor correct. clang-tidy cannot see the third-party API contract.

claim: clang-tidy bugprone-incorrect-roundings x6: engine/environment/terrain.cpp:398-400,493-495 casting (double + 0.5) to integer leads to incorrect rounding
rationale: The expression is static_cast<uint16_t>((n.x * 0.5f + 0.5f) * 65535.0f + 0.5f), the standard float-to-unorm16 normal encoding. n is a unit normal so each component is in [-1,1]; (n*0.5+0.5) maps to [0,1] and *65535 to [0,65535], so the value passed to the cast is always non-negative. The check's concern is truncation-toward-zero on NEGATIVE operands, which cannot occur here; for non-negative values truncating (x+0.5) IS round-to-nearest, identical to lround.

claim: pyright reportPossiblyUnboundVariable: tools/audit/lib/tier4_complexity.py:78 "lizard" possibly unbound, and tools/audit/lib/tier5_research.py:204 "DDGS" possibly unbound
rationale: Both use the try-import/HAS_X sentinel pattern with an early return before the use site. tier4_complexity.py sets HAS_LIZARD at lines 19-23 and returns at line 55 under "if not HAS_LIZARD"; line 78 is unreachable when lizard is unbound. tier5_research.py sets HAS_DDGS at lines 22-30 and returns at line 95 under "if not HAS_DDGS"; line 204 is unreachable when DDGS is unbound. Pyright does not correlate the sentinel flag with the bound-ness of the imported name.

claim: pyright reportAttributeAccessIssue: tools/audit/tests/test_audit_cli.py:25 "apply_no_color" is unknown import symbol
rationale: apply_no_color is defined at tools/audit/audit.py:47. The test reaches it via sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPT_DIR) at line 23 followed by "from audit import apply_no_color" at line 25; pyright does not model the runtime sys.path mutation, so it cannot resolve the module. Verified by running the file: "python3 -m pytest tests/test_audit_cli.py -q" reports 12 passed.

claim: clang-tidy: bugprone-suspicious-include at engine/audio/audio_music_player.cpp:22; bugprone-random-generator-seed at engine/audio/audio_engine.h:923; bugprone-branch-clone at engine/ui/game_screen.cpp:27
rationale: All three are intentional and documented at the site. audio_music_player.cpp:20-22 defines STB_VORBIS_HEADER_ONLY before including stb_vorbis.c — the upstream stb declarations-only idiom, with a comment saying implementation symbols come from external/stb/stb_vorbis_impl.cpp, mirroring audio_clip.cpp. audio_engine.h:923 is m_synthRng{1337u} for procedural audio synthesis, where a fixed seed is required for reproducible output and parity tests; it is not a security RNG. game_screen.cpp:26-27 returns GameScreen::Loading for both NewWalkthrough and Continue because both intents genuinely lead to the loading screen; the branches are distinct cases with the same correct target.

claim: Bulk static-analysis noise: ruff S101 x1427 (assert in tests), typos x8062 (71% inside binary assets, plus the LOD domain term x1385), cppcheck unusedStructMember x1012, bandit B602 shell=True at tools/audit/lib/utils.py:114
rationale: ruff S101: all 1427 hits are in test files, where assert is the assertion mechanism; S101 is a bandit rule aimed at production code. typos: 5747 of 8062 hits are byte sequences inside .jpg/.png/.hdr/.glb/.ttf binaries, and 1385 more are the domain term LOD (level of detail); after removing both, zero real misspellings remain in engine code. cppcheck unusedStructMember: this codebase is header-heavy and cppcheck analyses each TU in isolation, so members used from another translation unit read as unused. bandit B602: run_shell_cmd at utils.py:96-125 is a deliberate, isolated shell escape hatch for user config strings like "cd build && ctest"; it raises TypeError on any non-str argument and its docstring requires all other callers to use run_cmd. Input comes from the project's own audit_config.yaml, not untrusted data.

claim: shellcheck SC2001: scripts/check_changelog_pair.sh:72 "See if you can use ${variable//search/replace} instead" for echo "$affected" | sed 's/^/  /'
rationale: The sed call prefixes EVERY line of a multi-line string with two spaces, anchored on ^ with sed's per-line semantics. Bash parameter expansion has no per-line anchor: the nearest equivalent, ${affected//$'\n'/$'\n'  }, silently misses the first line and is markedly less readable. SC2001 is a style note aimed at single-token substitutions, and sed is the correct tool for this shape.
